title: Massacre (Ghallughara) Near Malerkotla, Kupp and Poheerd (The Singhs who were Khalsas in letter and spirit…

blocks.text: The way the Khalsa remained inexhaustible despite such carnage. So abundant remained the Khalsa (despite such massacre) As flows the water forever in a perennial stream. So naturally did the Singhs replace those who perished, As perennially gushing spring replaces the water that flowed. That the Khalsa expanded by the Divine Will, So has it been acknowledged by one and all. That those who had been inimical to the Khalsa, Had they been destroyed as one destroys the poisonous cacti. (1)
lines: The way the Khalsa remained inexhaustible despite such carnage.
So abundant remained the Khalsa (despite such massacre) As flows the water forever in a perennial stream.
So naturally did the Singhs replace those who perished,
As perennially gushing spring replaces the water that flowed.
That the Khalsa expanded by the Divine Will,
So has it been acknowledged by one and all.
That those who had been inimical to the Khalsa,
Had they been destroyed as one destroys the poisonous cacti.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Putting up their families in the (forested) Malwa region, Through plunder of Muslim troops did the Khalsa survive. Plundering the vanguard and the rearguard day and night, Thus did the Singhs harass the troops of Ahmad Shah Abdali. (2)
lines: Putting up their families in the (forested) Malwa region,
Through plunder of Muslim troops did the Khalsa survive.
Plundering the vanguard and the rearguard day and night,
Thus did the Singhs harass the troops of Ahmad Shah Abdali.

blocks.text: In the fort (of Ram Rauni) that the Singhs had raised at (Amritsar), Had Ahmad Shah Abdali put up a base camp in that fort. The most sacred and pious shrines which existed at Amritsar, Did Abdali's Pathan troops start razing to the ground. (3)
lines: In the fort (of Ram Rauni) that the Singhs had raised at (Amritsar),
Had Ahmad Shah Abdali put up a base camp in that fort.
The most sacred and pious shrines which existed at Amritsar,
Did Abdali's Pathan troops start razing to the ground.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Filling the sacred pool with the horses' dung, Abdali boasted of grazing his horses on the barley crop. The sanctum sanctorum of the holy Harmandar Sahib3 , Did Abdali blast with piling canisters filled with explosives. (4)
lines: Filling the sacred pool with the horses' dung,
Abdali boasted of grazing his horses on the barley crop.
The sanctum sanctorum of the holy Harmandar Sahib3 ,
Did Abdali blast with piling canisters filled with explosives.

blocks.text: As these explosive filled canisters were ignited with fire, An odd brick landed near Abdali after the explosion. As this brick struck straight at the nose of Abdali, For a lifetime was he rendered invalid, incurable for life. (5)
lines: As these explosive filled canisters were ignited with fire,
An odd brick landed near Abdali after the explosion.
As this brick struck straight at the nose of Abdali,
For a lifetime was he rendered invalid, incurable for life.

blocks.text: Thereafter, departing for Lahore after leaving Amritsar, Abdali did occupy the Mughal throne at Lahore. Hunting like hounds, he started killing the Singhs, Many a wicked deed thus did he commit indeed. (6)
lines: Thereafter, departing for Lahore after leaving Amritsar,
Abdali did occupy the Mughal throne at Lahore.
Hunting like hounds, he started killing the Singhs,
Many a wicked deed thus did he commit indeed.

blocks.text: Dohra:

While many Singhs sneaked into the Malwa region, So many others sought shelter in the wild growth. They kept on waylaying Afghans on their way to Kabul, As well as the Gilja Pathans even after walking upto Lahore. (7)
lines: While many Singhs sneaked into the Malwa region,
So many others sought shelter in the wild growth.
They kept on waylaying Afghans on their way to Kabul,
As well as the Gilja Pathans even after walking upto Lahore.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As Abdali was harassed by the Singhs beyond endurance, He dispatched a battery of soldiers to hunt down the Singhs. Even that squadron was waylaid by the Singhs, As day and night, the Singhs kept up the attacks. (8)
lines: As Abdali was harassed by the Singhs beyond endurance,
He dispatched a battery of soldiers to hunt down the Singhs.
Even that squadron was waylaid by the Singhs,
As day and night, the Singhs kept up the attacks.

blocks.text: As the Gilja Pathan troops slept at night with their faces down, The Singhs would steal their horses and get lost. Feeling highly incensed after hearing about these acts, Abdali contemplated of launching an attack on the Singhs. (9)
lines: As the Gilja Pathan troops slept at night with their faces down,
The Singhs would steal their horses and get lost.
Feeling highly incensed after hearing about these acts,
Abdali contemplated of launching an attack on the Singhs.

blocks.text: While Abdali favoured hunting the Singhs through the jungles, His minister opined that they would get humiliated after a chase. The minister cautioned him about the (brave) Majhail Singhs in thousands there, Equipped with the best of horses and the sharp shooters among them. (10)
lines: While Abdali favoured hunting the Singhs through the jungles,
His minister opined that they would get humiliated after a chase.
The minister cautioned him about the (brave) Majhail Singhs in thousands there,
Equipped with the best of horses and the sharp shooters among them.

blocks.text: The Pathan troops would die of thirst without water, As the Singhs would kill them with untold tortures. With the Singhs being natives and the Pathans being aliens, The Muslims should slaughter them with their united strength. (11)
lines: The Pathan troops would die of thirst without water,
As the Singhs would kill them with untold tortures.
With the Singhs being natives and the Pathans being aliens,
The Muslims should slaughter them with their united strength.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Feeling bitter, incensed and getting gripped with tension, Did Abdali's Pathan forces feel regret at the turn of events. Regretting that he who had ransacked whole of South and Eastern India, Had been outwitted and befuddled by the Singhs. (12)
lines: Feeling bitter, incensed and getting gripped with tension,
Did Abdali's Pathan forces feel regret at the turn of events.
Regretting that he who had ransacked whole of South and Eastern India,
Had been outwitted and befuddled by the Singhs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Fool that Abdali was, did he not realize this truth: How could the mighty Khalsa Panth be annihilated? As the ten Sikh Gurus had been at war with the Mughals, The roots of the Khalsa Panth were bound to get deeper. (13)
lines: Fool that Abdali was, did he not realize this truth: How could the mighty Khalsa Panth be annihilated?
As the ten Sikh Gurus had been at war with the Mughals,
The roots of the Khalsa Panth were bound to get deeper.

blocks.text: The more the Singhs fight and get killed, the more they multiply, No power on earth could uproot them and make them extinct. As the more one prunes a rose bush, the more it buds and flowers, The more the Khalsa is persecuted, the more it expands. (14)
lines: The more the Singhs fight and get killed, the more they multiply,
No power on earth could uproot them and make them extinct.
As the more one prunes a rose bush, the more it buds and flowers,
The more the Khalsa is persecuted, the more it expands.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Finding shelter in the Malwa region during this ordeal, The Singhs had to buy provisions for their survival. (With limited means), how could they survive without plundering, This was the issue which they discussed in their assemblies. (15)
lines: Finding shelter in the Malwa region during this ordeal,
The Singhs had to buy provisions for their survival.
(With limited means), how could they survive without plundering,
This was the issue which they discussed in their assemblies.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, organizing a religious congregation for this purpose, The Singhs initiated to launch an expedition for looting. Sending a contigent of Singhs for ransacking and waylaying, This Singh contingent created havoc around the city of Sirhind. (16)
lines: Thereupon, organizing a religious congregation for this purpose,
The Singhs initiated to launch an expedition for looting.
Sending a contigent of Singhs for ransacking and waylaying,
This Singh contingent created havoc around the city of Sirhind.

blocks.text: Forcing Jain Khan4 , the Sirhind custodian to retreat into his fort, The Singhs returned to put up a camp near Malerkotla. Someone among the Singhs suggested for taking over of Malerkotla, So that Malerkotla Pathan's nuisance could be put over for ever. (17)
lines: Forcing Jain Khan4 , the Sirhind custodian to retreat into his fort,
The Singhs returned to put up a camp near Malerkotla.
Someone among the Singhs suggested for taking over of Malerkotla,
So that Malerkotla Pathan's nuisance could be put over for ever.

blocks.text: While some favoured destroying Malerkotla there and then, Some others opposed this proposal of destroying Malerkotla. As Malerkotla had been worthy of (Tenth) Guru's grace5 , So no unanimity of opinion prevailed about Malerkotla's fate. (18)
lines: While some favoured destroying Malerkotla there and then,
Some others opposed this proposal of destroying Malerkotla.
As Malerkotla had been worthy of (Tenth) Guru's grace5 ,
So no unanimity of opinion prevailed about Malerkotla's fate.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As Malerkotla's Pathan rulers heard about this development, That Singhs were confabulating about attacking their city, They invited Jain Khan, the Sirhind custodian to Malerkotla, By dispatching messengers posthaste at the dead of night. (19)
lines: As Malerkotla's Pathan rulers heard about this development,
That Singhs were confabulating about attacking their city,
They invited Jain Khan, the Sirhind custodian to Malerkotla,
By dispatching messengers posthaste at the dead of night.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

They also sent messengers to Ahmad Shah Abdali, That the Singhs were stationed under their surveylance. While their joint troops would block the Singhs' exist from their side, Abdali's troops could attack the Singhs from their side at dawn. (20)
lines: They also sent messengers to Ahmad Shah Abdali,
That the Singhs were stationed under their surveylance.
While their joint troops would block the Singhs' exist from their side,
Abdali's troops could attack the Singhs from their side at dawn.

blocks.text: As their Muslim forces would block the Singh's passage from all sides, The Singhs would perish as easily as a papier-mache melts in rain. Hearing this, launching an expedition from Lahore. Abdali did put his up his first camp at Jandiala. (21)
lines: As their Muslim forces would block the Singh's passage from all sides,
The Singhs would perish as easily as a papier-mache melts in rain.
Hearing this, launching an expedition from Lahore.
Abdali did put his up his first camp at Jandiala.

blocks.text: Moving further, even as Abdali put up his second halt at Taiwan6 , The Singhs had no inkling about Pathan troops movement. So the Singhs' contingent moving further on their looting spree, They shifted from Raipur village towards Gujarwal village. (22)
lines: Moving further, even as Abdali put up his second halt at Taiwan6 ,
The Singhs had no inkling about Pathan troops movement.
So the Singhs' contingent moving further on their looting spree,
They shifted from Raipur village towards Gujarwal village.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Sending messenger (to his allies from his Taiwan Camp), Did Abdali summon Jain Khan and the Malerkotla Pathans. Promising to join his forces with theirs early in the morning, Did he reiterate his resolve to kill the Singhs after tracing them. (23)
lines: Sending messenger (to his allies from his Taiwan Camp),
Did Abdali summon Jain Khan and the Malerkotla Pathans.
Promising to join his forces with theirs early in the morning,
Did he reiterate his resolve to kill the Singhs after tracing them.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Muslim allies implemented their agreed plan the early morning, Truly did the Khalsa Panth forces fall on bad times. As the Singhs contingent was proceeding towards the river, From the front, did they come to face Ahmad Shah Abdali's troops. (24)
lines: As the Muslim allies implemented their agreed plan the early morning,
Truly did the Khalsa Panth forces fall on bad times.
As the Singhs contingent was proceeding towards the river,
From the front, did they come to face Ahmad Shah Abdali's troops.

blocks.text: As the Singhs spotted a swarm of red-coloured objects, They reckoned that kesu (Buteafrondosa) trees were in full bloom. But those who were old war veterans among the Singhs, They did identify the red shirts as Gijla Pathan troops. (25)
lines: As the Singhs spotted a swarm of red-coloured objects,
They reckoned that kesu (Buteafrondosa) trees were in full bloom.
But those who were old war veterans among the Singhs,
They did identify the red shirts as Gijla Pathan troops.

blocks.text: As the Singhs stopped their movement, dumbfounded with fear, The day-light did break upon the scene by that time. As the Gilja Pathans joined them on their (fast-running) horses, The Singhs had not even loaded their muskets by then. (26)
lines: As the Singhs stopped their movement, dumbfounded with fear,
The day-light did break upon the scene by that time.
As the Gilja Pathans joined them on their (fast-running) horses,
The Singhs had not even loaded their muskets by then.

blocks.text: So suddenly did the fight start with swords and arrows, So suddenly had the Pathan troops attacked the Singhs. Even then the Singhs stood their ground righting hard, As it was a war that they waged for their religion and ideology. (27)
lines: So suddenly did the fight start with swords and arrows,
So suddenly had the Pathan troops attacked the Singhs.
Even then the Singhs stood their ground righting hard,
As it was a war that they waged for their religion and ideology.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Free-booters and robbers who roamed the area for easy gains, Did all of them mingle with the Gilja Pathan troops. But a worst fate did these highway robbers meet indeed, As all of them were put to death by the Pathan troops. (28)
lines: Free-booters and robbers who roamed the area for easy gains,
Did all of them mingle with the Gilja Pathan troops.
But a worst fate did these highway robbers meet indeed,
As all of them were put to death by the Pathan troops.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Khalsa Panth troops started fighting with the Pathans, The Singh contingent that had gone ahead was asked to return. As the leading Singh contingent had to bear the main brunt, They suffered the maximum casualties in this battle. (29)
lines: As the Khalsa Panth troops started fighting with the Pathans,
The Singh contingent that had gone ahead was asked to return.
As the leading Singh contingent had to bear the main brunt,
They suffered the maximum casualties in this battle.

blocks.text: Assembling again and again (after retreating for a while), The Singhs kept on fighting with the Gilja Pathans. With the wielding of swords, spears, arrows, bows and muskets, There waged a fierce battle and killing from all the sides. (30)
lines: Assembling again and again (after retreating for a while),
The Singhs kept on fighting with the Gilja Pathans.
With the wielding of swords, spears, arrows, bows and muskets,
There waged a fierce battle and killing from all the sides.

blocks.text: After dealing with the main striking contingent of the Pathans, The leading Singh chiefs chalked out their further strategy. Towards the Malwa religion should they move their contingents, This was the information they sent through their Malwa representatives. (31)
lines: After dealing with the main striking contingent of the Pathans,
The leading Singh chiefs chalked out their further strategy.
Towards the Malwa religion should they move their contingents,
This was the information they sent through their Malwa representatives.

blocks.text: The Malwa Singhs should lead the Singhs towards their region, They must provide protection to the majority of Sikh troops. These representatives consisted of a Singh from Bhai ka Darraj village, The name of this Guru's devout Singh being Bhai Sangu Singh. (32)
lines: The Malwa Singhs should lead the Singhs towards their region,
They must provide protection to the majority of Sikh troops.
These representatives consisted of a Singh from Bhai ka Darraj village,
The name of this Guru's devout Singh being Bhai Sangu Singh.

blocks.text: The second representative was a police custodian of Ala Singh, His name being Sekhu Sngh from village Hambalwal. The third representative being Budha Singh Bhaika, These three representatives were deputed to lead the contingents. (33)
lines: The second representative was a police custodian of Ala Singh,
His name being Sekhu Sngh from village Hambalwal.
The third representative being Budha Singh Bhaika,
These three representatives were deputed to lead the contingents.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Tying a piece of cloth on the tip of their long spears, They made these appear as emblems of their contingents. Following these standard-bearers were Singh contingents, As they started their march towards the Malwa territory. (34)
lines: Tying a piece of cloth on the tip of their long spears,
They made these appear as emblems of their contingents.
Following these standard-bearers were Singh contingents,
As they started their march towards the Malwa territory.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Asking the Singh contingents to follow them on their tracks, Loudly did they shout these instructions to the contingents. As this fleet of Singh contingents marched after the Malwa representatives, The leading Singh contingents engaged the Pathan's striking contingent. (35)
lines: Asking the Singh contingents to follow them on their tracks,
Loudly did they shout these instructions to the contingents.
As this fleet of Singh contingents marched after the Malwa representatives,
The leading Singh contingents engaged the Pathan's striking contingent.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hardly had the Sikh caravan gone for three miles, When it was attacked by another enemy contingent. These were now the contingents of Jain Khan and Malerkotla chief, Which pounced upon the Sikh caravan with a rush. (36)
lines: Hardly had the Sikh caravan gone for three miles,
When it was attacked by another enemy contingent.
These were now the contingents of Jain Khan and Malerkotla chief,
Which pounced upon the Sikh caravan with a rush.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

This Sikh caravan had left unguarded and unprotected, As no Misl chief or warrior had accompanied, this caravan. So the Pathan and Mughal troops, blocking the caravan's movement, They attacked the (defenceless) caravan as a lion attacked a herd of sheep. (37)
lines: This Sikh caravan had left unguarded and unprotected,
As no Misl chief or warrior had accompanied, this caravan.
So the Pathan and Mughal troops, blocking the caravan's movement,
They attacked the (defenceless) caravan as a lion attacked a herd of sheep.

blocks.text: As many among them were slaughtered by the enemy troops, Those who survived ran back to join the Sikh contingents. Thereupon the Khalsa Panth leaders made a resolution, That the Sikh caravans must be accompanied by a warrior chief. (38)
lines: As many among them were slaughtered by the enemy troops,
Those who survived ran back to join the Sikh contingents.
Thereupon the Khalsa Panth leaders made a resolution,
That the Sikh caravans must be accompanied by a warrior chief.

blocks.text: Dohra:

There were S. Jassa Singh7 (Ahluwalia), and S. Sham Singh8 . Who had been the Misl chiefs of their contingents. Making them a joint appeal on behalf of all the Singhs, They were asked to accompany the Sikh caravans. (39)
lines: There were S.
Jassa Singh7 (Ahluwalia), and S.
Sham Singh8 .
Who had been the Misl chiefs of their contingents.
Making them a joint appeal on behalf of all the Singhs,
They were asked to accompany the Sikh caravans.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, S. Sham Singh did tell the Khalsa Panth, That he would take care of Jain Khan and Malerkotla troops. Asking the other chiefs to provide protection to the other three flanks, He exhorted them to fight this religio-ideological war determinedly. (40)
lines: Thereupon,
S.
Sham Singh did tell the Khalsa Panth,
That he would take care of Jain Khan and Malerkotla troops.
Asking the other chiefs to provide protection to the other three flanks,
He exhorted them to fight this religio-ideological war determinedly.

blocks.text: The Khalsa Panth having acceded to this exhortation and advice, S. Sham Singh marched towards the besieged caravan instantly. Leaving the remaining nine (misls) contingents to combat Abdali's troops, S. Sham Singh left on his mission after these instructions. (41)
lines: The Khalsa Panth having acceded to this exhortation and advice,
S.
Sham Singh marched towards the besieged caravan instantly.
Leaving the remaining nine (misls) contingents to combat Abdali's troops,
S.
Sham Singh left on his mission after these instructions.

blocks.text: Asking the Misl chiefs to keep beating their respective war-drums, They were asked to keep their contingental standards fluttering. Wherever they found the Muslim troops dominating in the battle, All the Singh contingents joined those formations to combat them. (42)
lines: Asking the Misl chiefs to keep beating their respective war-drums,
They were asked to keep their contingental standards fluttering.
Wherever they found the Muslim troops dominating in the battle,
All the Singh contingents joined those formations to combat them.

blocks.text: Dohra:

After delivering such instructions to other chiefs in this manner, S. Sham Singh soon caught up with Jain Khan and Malerkotla troops.. There he succeeded in making the Sikh caravan move further, After giving a good fight to the Gilja Pathan troops. (43)
lines: After delivering such instructions to other chiefs in this manner,
S.
Sham Singh soon caught up with Jain Khan and Malerkotla troops..
There he succeeded in making the Sikh caravan move further,
After giving a good fight to the Gilja Pathan troops.

blocks.text: Wielding their muskets, arrows and bows and mighty spears, Sham Singh's contingent warriors wielded their swords skillfully. Pushing their horses to barge into the enemy troops, The Singhs killed many of the mightiest among the Pathans. (44)
lines: Wielding their muskets, arrows and bows and mighty spears,
Sham Singh's contingent warriors wielded their swords skillfully.
Pushing their horses to barge into the enemy troops,
The Singhs killed many of the mightiest among the Pathans.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Soon did they push away Jain Khan's contingent away from caravan, After fighting a fierce battle with the Gilja Pathans. They also repulsed Luxmi Narayan's9 contingent of Pathans, After harassing and beating them to retreat. (45)
lines: Soon did they push away Jain Khan's contingent away from caravan,
After fighting a fierce battle with the Gilja Pathans.
They also repulsed Luxmi Narayan's9 contingent of Pathans,
After harassing and beating them to retreat.

blocks.text: . There being many mighty warriors among the Sham Singh's Misl, They threw away the Gilja Pathans by a volley of musket fires. Among these warriors were S. Karam Singh10 and Krora Singh" , As well as such warriors as S. Nahar Singh and Binda Singh. (46)
lines: There being many mighty warriors among the Sham Singh's Misl,
They threw away the Gilja Pathans by a volley of musket fires.
Among these warriors were S.
Karam Singh10 and Krora Singh" ,
As well as such warriors as S.
Nahar Singh and Binda Singh.

blocks.text: There being many such mighty warriors in this Misl contingent, They pushed away the Muslim troops away from the caravan. Jain Khan's contingent still kept up the fight with the Singhs, With such tactics as now retreating, now returning closer. (47)
lines: There being many such mighty warriors in this Misl contingent,
They pushed away the Muslim troops away from the caravan.
Jain Khan's contingent still kept up the fight with the Singhs,
With such tactics as now retreating, now returning closer.

blocks.text: Thereafter, summoning the services of Malwa Singh chiefs, Sham Singh asked them to lead the caravan towards Malwa. Listen further to the account of the other main contingents, Who kept on sometime retreating, sometime fighting tactfully. (48)
lines: Thereafter, summoning the services of Malwa Singh chiefs,
Sham Singh asked them to lead the caravan towards Malwa.
Listen further to the account of the other main contingents,
Who kept on sometime retreating, sometime fighting tactfully.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter, S. Charat Singh12 addressing the Khalsa Panth said: That they must pay heed to what he proposed to say. As Ahmad Shah Abdali had organized his troop formations, The Khalsa Panth, too, should reorganize their contingents. (49)
lines: Thereafter,
S.
Charat Singh12 addressing the Khalsa Panth said: That they must pay heed to what he proposed to say.
As Ahmad Shah Abdali had organized his troop formations,
The Khalsa Panth, too, should reorganize their contingents.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Making a combined formation of four Singh contingents, The Khalsa should deploy two contingents on both sides. Wherever the Mughal troops would appear to be dominating, He (Charat Singh) himself would rush to combat them. (50)
lines: Making a combined formation of four Singh contingents,
The Khalsa should deploy two contingents on both sides.
Wherever the Mughal troops would appear to be dominating,
He (Charat Singh) himself would rush to combat them.

blocks.text: By constituting such formations should the Singhs fight this battle, Otherwise they would not survive if they kept retreating. The Mughals possessed horses of a superior bread and greater stamina, While Singhs' horses could hardly run upto the nearest wild. (51)
lines: By constituting such formations should the Singhs fight this battle,
Otherwise they would not survive if they kept retreating.
The Mughals possessed horses of a superior bread and greater stamina,
While Singhs' horses could hardly run upto the nearest wild.

blocks.text: There were Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and a few other veteran Singhs, Who commented after listening to Charat Singh's proposal. As there was hardly any time for dividing Misls into new formations, They must keep on fighting jointly to protect the Khalsa Panth. (52)
lines: There were Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and a few other veteran Singhs,
Who commented after listening to Charat Singh's proposal.
As there was hardly any time for dividing Misls into new formations,
They must keep on fighting jointly to protect the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Muslims being far higher in numerical strength, the Singhs were in minority, They having the force of a whirlwind, the Singhs were a minor turbulence. So adopting a tactic of retreating and fighting and then retreating again, The Singhs must protect their caravan at all costs. (53)
lines: Muslims being far higher in numerical strength, the Singhs were in minority,
They having the force of a whirlwind, the Singhs were a minor turbulence.
So adopting a tactic of retreating and fighting and then retreating again,
The Singhs must protect their caravan at all costs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

So Charat Singh, too accepted the latest proposal, As was put forth by the elderly war veteran Singhs. Like the mighty lions did the Singhs combat the Pathans, Blocking their advance to protect the moving caravan. (54)
lines: So Charat Singh, too accepted the latest proposal,
As was put forth by the elderly war veteran Singhs.
Like the mighty lions did the Singhs combat the Pathans,
Blocking their advance to protect the moving caravan.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

For a selfless (communal) cause did the Singhs fight, From sacrificing their lives did they never shirk. For protecting the dignity and honour of Guru's Khalsa Panth, For the sake of their religion and ideology did they wage a war. (55)
lines: For a selfless (communal) cause did the Singhs fight,
From sacrificing their lives did they never shirk.
For protecting the dignity and honour of Guru's Khalsa Panth,
For the sake of their religion and ideology did they wage a war.

blocks.text: For a few hours, did the Singhs combat the Pathan troops, Like formidable pillars did they block the striking Pathan contingents. In the meantime, more contingents of the Pathan striking forces arrived, Which were commanded by Biland13 and Jahan Khan14 custodians. (56)
lines: For a few hours, did the Singhs combat the Pathan troops,
Like formidable pillars did they block the striking Pathan contingents.
In the meantime, more contingents of the Pathan striking forces arrived,
Which were commanded by Biland13 and Jahan Khan14 custodians.

blocks.text: These heavy reinforcements uprooted the combating Singhs as terribly , As a strong wind sweeps away the dry Bunyan tree leaves. Fighting retreating, stopping and returning did the Singhs keep combating, But being outnumbered by the Pathans, how long could they resist? (57)
lines: These heavy reinforcements uprooted the combating Singhs as terribly ,
As a strong wind sweeps away the dry Bunyan tree leaves.
Fighting retreating, stopping and returning did the Singhs keep combating,
But being outnumbered by the Pathans, how long could they resist?

blocks.text: Grinding and screeching his teeth in anger did Charat Singh fight, But Pathan troops being too many, desperately helpless did he feel. Retreating and fighting did the Singhs reach the Sikh caravan, Reaching the caravan, again did they stand to combat the Pathans. Truly did they protect the moving Sikh caravan from being invaded, Putting their own bodies in front of the invading Pathan troops. (58)
lines: Grinding and screeching his teeth in anger did Charat Singh fight,
But Pathan troops being too many, desperately helpless did he feel.
Retreating and fighting did the Singhs reach the Sikh caravan,
Reaching the caravan, again did they stand to combat the Pathans.
Truly did they protect the moving Sikh caravan from being invaded,
Putting their own bodies in front of the invading Pathan troops.

blocks.text: Dohra:

For a few hours more, did the Singhs keep blocking the Pathan forces, Thus allowing the Sikh caravan to keep moving ahead. But soon were they invaded with a rush from the rear, By the Pathan troops commanded by Ahmad Shah Abdali. (59)
lines: For a few hours more, did the Singhs keep blocking the Pathan forces,
Thus allowing the Sikh caravan to keep moving ahead.
But soon were they invaded with a rush from the rear,
By the Pathan troops commanded by Ahmad Shah Abdali.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Hardly had the Sikh caravan moved for four miles, With the Singhs fighting against Pathans at the rear guard. As Ahmad Shah Abdali himself attacked the Singhs, The raging dust made things invisible on the battlefield. (60)
lines: Hardly had the Sikh caravan moved for four miles,
With the Singhs fighting against Pathans at the rear guard.
As Ahmad Shah Abdali himself attacked the Singhs,
The raging dust made things invisible on the battlefield.

blocks.text: As the Singhs got lost in the raging din and dust, Their contingent kept running and advancing fast ahead. Ahmad Shah Abdali led four brigades of Pathan troops, Each brigade consisting of twelve thousand formidable horse riders. (61)
lines: As the Singhs got lost in the raging din and dust,
Their contingent kept running and advancing fast ahead.
Ahmad Shah Abdali led four brigades of Pathan troops,
Each brigade consisting of twelve thousand formidable horse riders.

blocks.text: Making a massive attack on this single Khalsa Panth contingent, They cut off the Khalsa contingent from the moving Sikh caravan.
As the caravan was rendered unprotected by the Singh contingent, Many Pathan troops entered and surrounded the Sikh caravan. (62)
lines: As the caravan was rendered unprotected by the Singh contingent,
Many Pathan troops entered and surrounded the Sikh caravan.

blocks.text: As the Khalsa contingent made another attempt to protect the caravan, For a moment, the Pathans' attention got diverted from the caravan. Making a dash, the Singhs from the rear rushed to the front, Where they were protected by the Singhs leading the caravan. (63)
lines: As the Khalsa contingent made another attempt to protect the caravan,
For a moment, the Pathans' attention got diverted from the caravan.
Making a dash, the Singhs from the rear rushed to the front,
Where they were protected by the Singhs leading the caravan.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Even then the Singhs kept up the fight while on the move, Protecting the Sikh caravan as much as they could from Pathans. Sometime fighting, sometime abandoning, sometime moving, Fleeing at times from the scene whenever they found it opportune. (64)
lines: Even then the Singhs kept up the fight while on the move,
Protecting the Sikh caravan as much as they could from Pathans.
Sometime fighting, sometime abandoning, sometime moving,
Fleeing at times from the scene whenever they found it opportune.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

With a dash did Abdali launch an attack, Separating the Khalsa Panth force from the caravan. As the caravan got alienated from the Singhs, Cutting through the caravan, Abdali divided it into two parts. (65)
lines: With a dash did Abdali launch an attack,
Separating the Khalsa Panth force from the caravan.
As the caravan got alienated from the Singhs,
Cutting through the caravan,
Abdali divided it into two parts.

blocks.text: As some from within the caravan also resisted and sacrificed, Rest of the caravan got a temporary relief for a while. As few more Singhs made an attempt to protect the caravan, They diverted the attention of the plundering Pathans. (66)
lines: As some from within the caravan also resisted and sacrificed,
Rest of the caravan got a temporary relief for a while.
As few more Singhs made an attempt to protect the caravan,
They diverted the attention of the plundering Pathans.

blocks.text: Once again with a rush Abdali made another attack, Cutting off another section from the main body of caravan. Under such an attack of sharp swords came the Sikh caravan, As the weeds fall under the sharp edges of the peasant's hoe. (67)
lines: Once again with a rush Abdali made another attack,
Cutting off another section from the main body of caravan.
Under such an attack of sharp swords came the Sikh caravan,
As the weeds fall under the sharp edges of the peasant's hoe.

blocks.text: As a farmer gets his crop harvested by a body of chartered peasants, Who harvest his crop so speedily in a competitive spirit, So did the Gilja Pathan troops would cut through the caravan, Sparing an odd Sikh who would flee from the caravan. (68)
lines: As a farmer gets his crop harvested by a body of chartered peasants,
Who harvest his crop so speedily in a competitive spirit,
So did the Gilja Pathan troops would cut through the caravan,
Sparing an odd Sikh who would flee from the caravan.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter, did Ahmed Shah Abdali resolve in his mind, That without laying a siege would the Singhs not get destroyed. Somehow or the other must the Singhs be encircled in, Then alone could they be beaten into submission. (69)
lines: Thereafter, did Ahmed Shah Abdali resolve in his mind,
That without laying a siege would the Singhs not get destroyed.
Somehow or the other must the Singhs be encircled in,
Then alone could they be beaten into submission.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, soon did Abdali dispatch his messengers posthaste, Lodging a strong protest to Jain Khan regarding his promised support, Abdali accused him of not standing up to what he had promised, As he had failed to block the Singhs' movement from the front. (70)
lines: Thereupon, soon did Abdali dispatch his messengers posthaste,
Lodging a strong protest to Jain Khan regarding his promised support,
Abdali accused him of not standing up to what he had promised,
As he had failed to block the Singhs' movement from the front.

blocks.text: With twenty thousand horses was Jain Khan's army provided, Had those been snatched and minimized by the Singhs? With the troops of Laxmi Narayan and Malerkotla was he assisted, Could he not take over the Singhs despite such a large force? (71)
lines: With twenty thousand horses was Jain Khan's army provided,
Had those been snatched and minimized by the Singhs?
With the troops of Laxmi Narayan and Malerkotla was he assisted,
Could he not take over the Singhs despite such a large force?

blocks.text: If he (Jain Khan) could check the Singhs' movement from the front, Abdali's own troops would eliminate the Singhs in a few hours. Without getting encircled and blocked would the Singhs be not eliminated, Such a conclusion he had arrived at after a thorough deliberation. (72)
lines: If he (Jain Khan) could check the Singhs' movement from the front,
Abdali's own troops would eliminate the Singhs in a few hours.
Without getting encircled and blocked would the Singhs be not eliminated,
Such a conclusion he had arrived at after a thorough deliberation.

blocks.text: Highly incensed did Jain Khan feel after listening to Abdali's rebuff, As a sleeping lion gets disturbed from his deep slumber. As he made a dash to block and check the Singhs' advance, He was repulsed by a counter attack by Sham Singh's contingent. (73)
lines: Highly incensed did Jain Khan feel after listening to Abdali's rebuff,
As a sleeping lion gets disturbed from his deep slumber.
As he made a dash to block and check the Singhs' advance,
He was repulsed by a counter attack by Sham Singh's contingent.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter, did Jain Khan sent a report to Ahmad Shah Abdali, Impossible it was to check the Singhs from the front. Fewer though they appeared to be in numerical strength, So many more they proved in strength during fight. (74)
lines: Thereafter, did Jain Khan sent a report to Ahmad Shah Abdali,
Impossible it was to check the Singhs from the front.
Fewer though they appeared to be in numerical strength,
So many more they proved in strength during fight.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, did Jain Khan report to Ahmad Shah Abdali, In no way could he block the Singhs' passage, such dare devils they were. Suggesting Abdali to attack the Singhs instead of invading the caravan, Let the Mughal Pathan force first slaughter the fighting Singhs. (75)
lines: Thereafter, did Jain Khan report to Ahmad Shah Abdali,
In no way could he block the Singhs' passage, such dare devils they were.
Suggesting Abdali to attack the Singhs instead of invading the caravan,
Let the Mughal Pathan force first slaughter the fighting Singhs.

blocks.text: Accepting Jain Khan's proposal after listening to his plan, Abdali did launch an attack on the Khalsa Panth force. Opening a volley of bullets after taking up positions, A few Singhs did kill those who dared to attack them. (76)
lines: Accepting Jain Khan's proposal after listening to his plan,
Abdali did launch an attack on the Khalsa Panth force.
Opening a volley of bullets after taking up positions,
A few Singhs did kill those who dared to attack them.

blocks.text: As the Singhs observed Ahmad Shah Abdali's force approaching, They started retreating from the positions they had taken. From the small fire-arms did the Singhs keep firing while retreating,, Thus killing those who dared to venture too near to them. (77)
lines: As the Singhs observed Ahmad Shah Abdali's force approaching,
They started retreating from the positions they had taken.
From the small fire-arms did the Singhs keep firing while retreating,,
Thus killing those who dared to venture too near to them.

blocks.text: How could such a huge army of Ahmed Shah Abdali be finished, Which invaded as if a massive tidal wave rose from the sea. Retreating, thus, did the Singhs keep moving for a mile and a half, When they stopped the pursing again to combat Abdali's troops. (78)
lines: How could such a huge army of Ahmed Shah Abdali be finished,
Which invaded as if a massive tidal wave rose from the sea.
Retreating, thus, did the Singhs keep moving for a mile and a half,
When they stopped the pursing again to combat Abdali's troops.

blocks.text: Dohra:

During this massive invasion (of the combined Mughal Pathans troops), S. Charat Singh remained present within the caravan. Fighting back and forth both in the front and the rearguard, He kept on making way for the caravan to move ahead. (79)
lines: During this massive invasion (of the combined Mughal Pathans troops),
S.
Charat Singh remained present within the caravan.
Fighting back and forth both in the front and the rearguard,
He kept on making way for the caravan to move ahead.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At this stage, S. Jassa Singh (Ahluwalia) taking up a very stubborn stand, Ordered his contingent to stop retreating, after a heated argument. The troops, pleaded with him to let them retreat a bit more, As they would be wiped out if they ventured to stop their retreat. (80)
lines: At this stage,
S.
Jassa Singh (Ahluwalia) taking up a very stubborn stand,
Ordered his contingent to stop retreating, after a heated argument.
The troops, pleaded with him to let them retreat a bit more,
As they would be wiped out if they ventured to stop their retreat.

blocks.text: Many a wound did Jassa Singh receive on his body, As he was hit at many places by arrows, bullets and swords. He had been attacking as well as taking others' attack upon himself, With head-on-collision had his horse been confronting enemy horses. (81)
lines: Many a wound did Jassa Singh receive on his body,
As he was hit at many places by arrows, bullets and swords.
He had been attacking as well as taking others' attack upon himself,
With head-on-collision had his horse been confronting enemy horses.

blocks.text: Exhausted and drained of energy had Jassa Singh's horse been rendered, As too much running had it been doing during the ongoing fighting, Spur as much as Jassa Singh could do with his heels, Not an inch could his horse move, so drained it was. (82)
lines: Exhausted and drained of energy had Jassa Singh's horse been rendered,
As too much running had it been doing during the ongoing fighting,
Spur as much as Jassa Singh could do with his heels,
Not an inch could his horse move, so drained it was.

blocks.text: Dohra:

There was one adopted son of Jassa Singh (Ahluwalia), Who was known by the name of Gurmukh Singh. Pleading before his mentor, thus did he say to him, No purpose would it serve to combat single handedly. (83)
lines: There was one adopted son of Jassa Singh (Ahluwalia),
Who was known by the name of Gurmukh Singh.
Pleading before his mentor, thus did he say to him,
No purpose would it serve to combat single handedly.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

By standing and combating would they never survive, Then why should they get killed in that unequal fight? Thereupon Jassa Singh told his disciple in such a vein, That his horse had failed to move ahead anymore. (84)
lines: By standing and combating would they never survive,
Then why should they get killed in that unequal fight?
Thereupon Jassa Singh told his disciple in such a vein,
That his horse had failed to move ahead anymore.

blocks.text: Thereupon, picking up a whiplash and dashing it in the air, Gurumukh Singh wished to flog Jassa Singh's horse. Thereupon, Jassa Singh prohibited his disciple with a remark, That did the latter wish to demean his status among the Singhs? (85)
lines: Thereupon, picking up a whiplash and dashing it in the air,
Gurumukh Singh wished to flog Jassa Singh's horse.
Thereupon,
Jassa Singh prohibited his disciple with a remark,
That did the latter wish to demean his status among the Singhs?

blocks.text: Would he not become a butt of ridicule among the Khalsa Panth, Getting accused of deserting the field after getting his horse flogged? With what face would he sit among Khalsa congregation, Getting ridiculed for cowardice by his own Khalsa fraternity? (86)
lines: Would he not become a butt of ridicule among the Khalsa Panth,
Getting accused of deserting the field after getting his horse flogged?
With what face would he sit among Khalsa congregation,
Getting ridiculed for cowardice by his own Khalsa fraternity?

blocks.text: He who had been declared a Sovereign among the Khalsa Panth, Did his disciple wish him to be branded a coward? Death, indeed, was preferable to such a life of indignity, Which, at least, would grant him some honour at least. (87)
lines: He who had been declared a Sovereign among the Khalsa Panth,
Did his disciple wish him to be branded a coward?
Death, indeed, was preferable to such a life of indignity,
Which, at least, would grant him some honour at least.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Sparing his own horse for his superior after dismounting, Gurmukh Singh made Jassa Singh mount his own horse. Fighting, resisting, combating and still marching ahead, Gurmukh Singh kept on braving all blows on his person. (88)
lines: Sparing his own horse for his superior after dismounting,
Gurmukh Singh made Jassa Singh mount his own horse.
Fighting, resisting, combating and still marching ahead,
Gurmukh Singh kept on braving all blows on his person.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Full twenty two wounds did Jassa Singh receive on his person, Still did Jassa Singh keep on righting with the enemy. The moment they heard of sovereign Jassa Singh's getting wounded, Immensely shocked did all the Singh chiefs15 feel at this news. (89)
lines: Full twenty two wounds did Jassa Singh receive on his person,
Still did Jassa Singh keep on righting with the enemy.
The moment they heard of sovereign Jassa Singh's getting wounded,
Immensely shocked did all the Singh chiefs15 feel at this news.

blocks.text: Among their contingents did all the contingent chiefs stand, Which included the Bhangi, Ghaniya and Ramgarhia chiefs. The Nakkais, Nishan-walias and Dallewalias were also there, Besides Nawab Kapoor Singh and Ahluwalia Misl chiefs. (90)
lines: Among their contingents did all the contingent chiefs stand,
Which included the Bhangi,
Ghaniya and Ramgarhia chiefs.
The Nakkais,
Nishan-walias and Dallewalias were also there,
Besides Nawab Kapoor Singh and Ahluwalia Misl chiefs.

blocks.text: Among these stood chiefs of Shukarchakia and Sham Singh's misl, As well the devout militant chiefs of Nihang Singh's Misl. The Singh chief of Amritsari and Anandpuri contingents, Were there along with Ramdasia Ranghretta Singhs and Masand chiefs. (91)
lines: Among these stood chiefs of Shukarchakia and Sham Singh's misl,
As well the devout militant chiefs of Nihang Singh's Misl.
The Singh chief of Amritsari and Anandpuri contingents,
Were there along with Ramdasia Ranghretta Singhs and Masand chiefs.

blocks.text: The other chiefs from the Bedi, Sodhi and Trehan castes, Who had also included themselves among the Khalsa Panth. All these Singhs kept on getting wounded and sacrificing themselves, Sometime standing to combat the enemy sometime moving ahead. (92)
lines: The other chiefs from the Bedi,
Sodhi and Trehan castes,
Who had also included themselves among the Khalsa Panth.
All these Singhs kept on getting wounded and sacrificing themselves,
Sometime standing to combat the enemy sometime moving ahead.

blocks.text: Dohra:

All the Sikh contingents, be they large or small in strength, Stood in perfect readiness to fight wielding their weapons. They took a vow to move from their point of their posting, Only after each one of them had killed one two Pathans. (93)
lines: All the Sikh contingents, be they large or small in strength,
Stood in perfect readiness to fight wielding their weapons.
They took a vow to move from their point of their posting,
Only after each one of them had killed one two Pathans.

blocks.text: At that moment, some one passed a taunting remark, That S. Charat Singh had claimed himself to be so brave. He had boasted that he alone would fight at a spot, Wherever Ahmad Shah Abdali was spotted in the field. (94)
lines: At that moment, some one passed a taunting remark,
That S.
Charat Singh had claimed himself to be so brave.
He had boasted that he alone would fight at a spot,
Wherever Ahmad Shah Abdali was spotted in the field.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Feeling stung at these insinuating remarks by a Singh, S. Charat Singh did kick his horse towards Ahmad Shah Abdali. Failing to locate him in the field upto a long distance, He could not see through the raging dust too far. (95)
lines: Feeling stung at these insinuating remarks by a Singh,
S.
Charat Singh did kick his horse towards Ahmad Shah Abdali.
Failing to locate him in the field upto a long distance,
He could not see through the raging dust too far.

blocks.text: After a thorough search did Charat Singh return to the caravan, Still slaughtering the Gilja Pathans with his sword's blows. As his hand got exhausted by wielding his heavy sword, He did pick up a spear to carry on his fight. (96)
lines: After a thorough search did Charat Singh return to the caravan,
Still slaughtering the Gilja Pathans with his sword's blows.
As his hand got exhausted by wielding his heavy sword,
He did pick up a spear to carry on his fight.

blocks.text: As even the blade of his spear also broke into pieces, He did pick up a small fire arm to shoot the enemy. As even his exhausted horse had to be changed for him, He did stop for a while to put a bandage on his wounds. (97)
lines: As even the blade of his spear also broke into pieces,
He did pick up a small fire arm to shoot the enemy.
As even his exhausted horse had to be changed for him,
He did stop for a while to put a bandage on his wounds.

blocks.text: Gathering his whole contingent once again with him, Many a Gilja Pathan soldiers did he kill and slaughter. Whenever, the caravan came under a heavy enemy attack, S. Charat Singh would himself jump into the fray to combat. (98)
lines: Gathering his whole contingent once again with him,
Many a Gilja Pathan soldiers did he kill and slaughter.
Whenever, the caravan came under a heavy enemy attack,
S.
Charat Singh would himself jump into the fray to combat.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Killing so many Gilja Pathans (with his concerted efforts), Many a Sikh lives did Charat Singh save so far. Catching hold of so many horses of the dead Gilja Pathans, Many a Singh foot soldiers did he mount on these. (99)
lines: Killing so many Gilja Pathans (with his concerted efforts),
Many a Sikh lives did Charat Singh save so far.
Catching hold of so many horses of the dead Gilja Pathans,
Many a Singh foot soldiers did he mount on these.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Hardly could anyone fight as bravely as Charat Singh did, Instantly would he reach those who dared to challenge him. Stopping, moving, fighting never would he leave the caravan, Quickly would he move ahead and then return again. (100)
lines: Hardly could anyone fight as bravely as Charat Singh did,
Instantly would he reach those who dared to challenge him.
Stopping, moving, fighting never would he leave the caravan,
Quickly would he move ahead and then return again.

blocks.text: Leaving his contingent sometime he would attack single handed, Soon would be return after killing some Gilja Pathans. His contingent too would take many risks after him, Tactfully would he push those into wilds who got wounded. (101)
lines: Leaving his contingent sometime he would attack single handed,
Soon would be return after killing some Gilja Pathans.
His contingent too would take many risks after him,
Tactfully would he push those into wilds who got wounded.

blocks.text: Many a Singh would be prod to move to the front, To many of them would he lend his fast running horses. Thus managing to guard his people in the caravan, Many a life did he save (through his grit and tact). (102)
lines: Many a Singh would be prod to move to the front,
To many of them would he lend his fast running horses.
Thus managing to guard his people in the caravan,
Many a life did he save (through his grit and tact).

blocks.text: As fiercely would he attack upon the Pathan hordes, As a ferocious falcon pounces upon a pack of migratory birds. Injuring someone at one place and someone at two places, He kept running and fighting from one flank to the other. (103)
lines: As fiercely would he attack upon the Pathan hordes,
As a ferocious falcon pounces upon a pack of migratory birds.
Injuring someone at one place and someone at two places,
He kept running and fighting from one flank to the other.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Like a fast running water spider did horses run back and forth, Like a flash of lightening would Charat Singh enter the Pathan forces. The Singhs would wipe out the Gilja Pathan troops (as perfectly), As one's noble deeds wipe out all traces of one's sins. (104)
lines: Like a fast running water spider did horses run back and forth,
Like a flash of lightening would Charat Singh enter the Pathan forces.
The Singhs would wipe out the Gilja Pathan troops (as perfectly),
As one's noble deeds wipe out all traces of one's sins.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At no cost would the Singh run away from the caravan, At all costs would he protect it though himself getting wounded. Blood-soaked did his garments turn blood-red, As if he had participated in the (Hola) festival of colours. (105)
lines: At no cost would the Singh run away from the caravan,
At all costs would he protect it though himself getting wounded.
Blood-soaked did his garments turn blood-red,
As if he had participated in the (Hola) festival of colours.

blocks.text: Keeping a reserve of five fast running steeds for his exclusive use, Would S. Charat Singh keep on changing horses one after another. Though many a wound did S. Charat Singh receive on his body, He kept on fighting without feeling frustrated by so many wounds. (106)
lines: Keeping a reserve of five fast running steeds for his exclusive use,
Would S.
Charat Singh keep on changing horses one after another.
Though many a wound did S.
Charat Singh receive on his body,
He kept on fighting without feeling frustrated by so many wounds.

blocks.text: Going ahead, would he keep on firing from his firearm, He would kill another Pathan after shooting one already. After emptying one musket of the loaded ammunition, He would snatch another one from one of his comrades. (107)
lines: Going ahead, would he keep on firing from his firearm,
He would kill another Pathan after shooting one already.
After emptying one musket of the loaded ammunition,
He would snatch another one from one of his comrades.

blocks.text: Among all the ace-shooters was he reckoned to be most superior, As he fired as many bullets single handed as did the whole contingent. Any one who claimed himself to be the most skilled shooter, Was not indeed half as skilled as was S. Charat Singh. (108)
lines: Among all the ace-shooters was he reckoned to be most superior,
As he fired as many bullets single handed as did the whole contingent.
Any one who claimed himself to be the most skilled shooter,
Was not indeed half as skilled as was S.
Charat Singh.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Such indeed was the reputation of S. Charat Singh as a sharp shooter, That he became very famous worldwide for his shooting skill. His shot was as effective from a point blank range, As he did when he fired from a long distance. (109)
lines: Such indeed was the reputation of S.
Charat Singh as a sharp shooter,
That he became very famous worldwide for his shooting skill.
His shot was as effective from a point blank range,
As he did when he fired from a long distance.

blocks.text: Fighting, killing, and getting killed thus so speedily, The caravan did move further for a mile or so. Thereafter, did Ahmad Shah Abdali himself arrive, And launched a massive attack on the Singhs. (110)
lines: Fighting, killing, and getting killed thus so speedily,
The caravan did move further for a mile or so.
Thereafter, did Ahmad Shah Abdali himself arrive,
And launched a massive attack on the Singhs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

With a massive force did Abdali push away the Singhs, Thereafter surrounding the caravan with a large army. The caravan carried two copies of holy Guru Granth Sahib, One written at Amritsar, the other composed at Dam Dama Sahib. (Ill) Blocking the caravan's movement from the front, Abdali divided the whole caravan into two separate parts. Carrying the Amritsari version did Majhail Singhs fight, Who were always armed with several weapons. (112)
lines: With a massive force did Abdali push away the Singhs,
Thereafter surrounding the caravan with a large army.
The caravan carried two copies of holy Guru Granth Sahib,
One written at Amritsar, the other composed at Dam Dama Sahib.
(Ill) Blocking the caravan's movement from the front,
Abdali divided the whole caravan into two separate parts.
Carrying the Amritsari version did Majhail Singhs fight,
Who were always armed with several weapons.

blocks.text: Killing these Majhail Singhs after a small fight, Abdali's troops attacked Malwa Singhs carrying Damdami verson. Fighting for a while they also perished in this battle, As they were helpless without having any weapons. (113)
lines: Killing these Majhail Singhs after a small fight,
Abdali's troops attacked Malwa Singhs carrying Damdami verson.
Fighting for a while they also perished in this battle,
As they were helpless without having any weapons.

blocks.text: Taking it as a war for upholding their religion and ideology, The Singhs carried on the fight even with sticks and stones. But as sticks and stones could hardly beat the enemy, The Pathan troops kept on slaughtering Singhs with their swords. (114)
lines: Taking it as a war for upholding their religion and ideology,
The Singhs carried on the fight even with sticks and stones.
But as sticks and stones could hardly beat the enemy,
The Pathan troops kept on slaughtering Singhs with their swords.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Killing and getting killed in this unequal battle, The caravan did reach the vicinity of village Gahal16 . Sometime combating the Pathans by entering the caravan, Sometime would the Singhs run quickly from the scene. (115)
lines: Killing and getting killed in this unequal battle,
The caravan did reach the vicinity of village Gahal16 .
Sometime combating the Pathans by entering the caravan,
Sometime would the Singhs run quickly from the scene.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the caravan looked up to the village for a succour, The village inhabitants barred and locked their doors. As the villagers refused the caravan to enter the village, The caravan really had to face hard times. (116)
lines: As the caravan looked up to the village for a succour,
The village inhabitants barred and locked their doors.
As the villagers refused the caravan to enter the village,
The caravan really had to face hard times.

blocks.text: Those who took shelter inside the stacks of cow-dung cakes, They were killed by the chasing Gilja Pathan soldiers. Those who ventured to sneak into homes of scheduled caste residents, They were also forced to get out by the householders. (117)
lines: Those who took shelter inside the stacks of cow-dung cakes,
They were killed by the chasing Gilja Pathan soldiers.
Those who ventured to sneak into homes of scheduled caste residents,
They were also forced to get out by the householders.

blocks.text: As corpse upon corpse piled up during this massacre, Some of them survived who fell underneath the corpses. As the robbers started searching the dead for any valuables, Those odd survivors were also killed by the looters. (118)
lines: As corpse upon corpse piled up during this massacre,
Some of them survived who fell underneath the corpses.
As the robbers started searching the dead for any valuables,
Those odd survivors were also killed by the looters.

blocks.text: Dohra:

There were many stacks of harvested dry stalks, Of animal fodder crops such as sorghum and millet. Those who hid themselves in these harvested haystacks, They were burnt alive by setting these stacks on fire. (119)
lines: There were many stacks of harvested dry stalks,
Of animal fodder crops such as sorghum and millet.
Those who hid themselves in these harvested haystacks,
They were burnt alive by setting these stacks on fire.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Feeling highly enraged at this massacre of his people, S. Charat Singh did reach the (defenders) caravan. As five musketeers kept on loading the muskets, He kept on killing Gilja Pathans with his sure shots. (120)
lines: Feeling highly enraged at this massacre of his people,
S.
Charat Singh did reach the (defenders) caravan.
As five musketeers kept on loading the muskets,
He kept on killing Gilja Pathans with his sure shots.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Being devastated by both hunger and thirst there, Did Ahmad Shah Abdali stop to drink water. As this chasing and massacring slowed down a bit, Did the Sikh caravan move ahead of the resting Pathans. (121)
lines: Being devastated by both hunger and thirst there,
Did Ahmad Shah Abdali stop to drink water.
As this chasing and massacring slowed down a bit,
Did the Sikh caravan move ahead of the resting Pathans.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Though with the Indian heat did Abdali's troops feel harassed, The Khalsa Singhs felt no impact of this oppressive heat. As Jahan Khan (the Sirhind custodian) came in hot pursuit, He was seriously wounded by the combating Singhs. (122)
lines: Though with the Indian heat did Abdali's troops feel harassed,
The Khalsa Singhs felt no impact of this oppressive heat.
As Jahan Khan (the Sirhind custodian) came in hot pursuit,
He was seriously wounded by the combating Singhs.

blocks.text: Marching past the village Gahal, the Singhs did start fighting again, Despite Pathans' massive attack, the Singhs did put up a brave fight. Providing protection to those who survived in the caravan, The Singhs guarded the caravan from both the flanks. (123)
lines: Marching past the village Gahal, the Singhs did start fighting again,
Despite Pathans' massive attack, the Singhs did put up a brave fight.
Providing protection to those who survived in the caravan,
The Singhs guarded the caravan from both the flanks.

blocks.text: As a mother hen protects her newly hatched chicks, She spreads both her wings to keep her brood protected. So did Khalsa Panth Singhs provide protection to the caravan, Making the survivors march ahead of the armed Singhs. (124)
lines: As a mother hen protects her newly hatched chicks,
She spreads both her wings to keep her brood protected.
So did Khalsa Panth Singhs provide protection to the caravan,
Making the survivors march ahead of the armed Singhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the moving caravan reached a set of two villages, Which were known by the names of Kutabo-Brahmini17 . Many from the caravan did sneak into these villages, As soon as they looked at these two villages. (125)
lines: As the moving caravan reached a set of two villages,
Which were known by the names of Kutabo-Brahmini17 .
Many from the caravan did sneak into these villages,
As soon as they looked at these two villages.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The village residents being subjects of Malkerkotla Pathan ruler, The Malerkotla Pathan troops laid a siege to the villages. As the villagers were ordered by the Malerkotla Pathans, They started looting and killing the Sikh caravan. (126)
lines: The village residents being subjects of Malkerkotla Pathan ruler,
The Malerkotla Pathan troops laid a siege to the villages.
As the villagers were ordered by the Malerkotla Pathans,
They started looting and killing the Sikh caravan.

blocks.text: As the villagers came out hearing the beat of a drum, They also started chasing the defenceless caravan. As desperate cries and shrieks arose from the helpless caravan, S. Charat Singh heard these heart-rending cries of his fellow men. (127)
lines: As the villagers came out hearing the beat of a drum,
They also started chasing the defenceless caravan.
As desperate cries and shrieks arose from the helpless caravan,
S.
Charat Singh heard these heart-rending cries of his fellow men.

blocks.text: With a mighty dash did he attack the plundering villagers, Many a Muslim converts (Ranghars) did he kill with a sword, Providing adequate protection to the beleaguered Singhs, The Muslim converts (Ranghars) did he kill so thoroughly. (128)
lines: With a mighty dash did he attack the plundering villagers,
Many a Muslim converts (Ranghars) did he kill with a sword,
Providing adequate protection to the beleaguered Singhs,
The Muslim converts (Ranghars) did he kill so thoroughly.

blocks.text: Outside the villages, whosoever did the Singhs come across, He got severely beaten and killed by the defiant Singhs. After killing these villagers, did S. Charat Singh join his contingent, Resuming his attack on the invading Gilja Pathans. Thereafter, the wise elderly Singhs did forbid him, That confrontation at that juncture was not in Khalsa's interest. (129)
lines: Outside the villages, whosoever did the Singhs come across,
He got severely beaten and killed by the defiant Singhs.
After killing these villagers, did S.
Charat Singh join his contingent,
Resuming his attack on the invading Gilja Pathans.
Thereafter, the wise elderly Singhs did forbid him,
That confrontation at that juncture was not in Khalsa's interest.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Gilja Pathan troops having been exhausted by now, They also put a stop to fighting and chasing, But the defiant Singhs did not stop fighting, As they had refreshed themselves after taking water. (130)
lines: The Gilja Pathan troops having been exhausted by now,
They also put a stop to fighting and chasing,
But the defiant Singhs did not stop fighting,
As they had refreshed themselves after taking water.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As all the Singhs stood defiant there despite all odds, They had covered a distance of twelve miles with the caravan. As they had run for one hundred miles from Lahore to this place, So Abdali's Pathan troops felt defeated in their mission. (131)
lines: As all the Singhs stood defiant there despite all odds,
They had covered a distance of twelve miles with the caravan.
As they had run for one hundred miles from Lahore to this place,
So Abdali's Pathan troops felt defeated in their mission.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Summer's hot sun reached the midday position, The summer heat was scorching in its hottest intensity. As the troops kept running, fighting, standing and fighting again, They desperately yearned for resting and slaking their thirst. (132)
lines: As the Summer's hot sun reached the midday position,
The summer heat was scorching in its hottest intensity.
As the troops kept running, fighting, standing and fighting again,
They desperately yearned for resting and slaking their thirst.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
As both horses as well as men were thirsty for want of water, Their throats were parched with thirst and searing heat.
As they could hardly come across any water reservoir, They could not take it even if they came upon any source. (133)
lines: As they could hardly come across any water reservoir,
They could not take it even if they came upon any source.

blocks.text: For the last twelve miles, they had not spotted water anywhere, Though troops from both sides were desperately in need of water. As all of them spotted a water reservoir nearby, All of them felt as if they had got a new lease of life. (134)
lines: For the last twelve miles, they had not spotted water anywhere,
Though troops from both sides were desperately in need of water.
As all of them spotted a water reservoir nearby,
All of them felt as if they had got a new lease of life.

blocks.text: Seeing a huge water reservoir, both rushed towards it, Both Singhs and Pathans ran for water being desperately thirsty. Even the unarmed members of the caravan yearned to take water, Hardly mindful were they of the sword blows of the Pathans. (135)
lines: Seeing a huge water reservoir, both rushed towards it,
Both Singhs and Pathans ran for water being desperately thirsty.
Even the unarmed members of the caravan yearned to take water,
Hardly mindful were they of the sword blows of the Pathans.

blocks.text: Even the Gilja Pathans forgot to fight for a while, As they also rushed to take water towards the reservoir. Extreme thirst would make them run for taking water, Hardly caring whether they lived or died during the attempt. (136)
lines: Even the Gilja Pathans forgot to fight for a while,
As they also rushed to take water towards the reservoir.
Extreme thirst would make them run for taking water,
Hardly caring whether they lived or died during the attempt.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then did the Malwa Singhs tell the other Singh contingents, That no water was available ahead for a long distance. Whosoever moved from there without taking water, Surely would he die of thirst on the way ahead. (137)
lines: Then did the Malwa Singhs tell the other Singh contingents,
That no water was available ahead for a long distance.
Whosoever moved from there without taking water,
Surely would he die of thirst on the way ahead.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, the Khalsa Panth Singhs standing for a while, confabulated, That they must ensure that every one must drink water. That the Singhs must make sacrifices for their brethren in the caravan, That they must protect the Sikh caravan even at the cost of their lives. (138)
lines: Thereupon, the Khalsa Panth Singhs standing for a while, confabulated,
That they must ensure that every one must drink water.
That the Singhs must make sacrifices for their brethren in the caravan,
That they must protect the Sikh caravan even at the cost of their lives.

blocks.text: After this resolution, did the Khalsa Singhs stand guard, So that no Gilja Pathan soldier set foot on their territory. With the protection provided by Singh on both the sides, All the other Singhs joined their contingents after drinking water. (139)
lines: After this resolution, did the Khalsa Singhs stand guard,
So that no Gilja Pathan soldier set foot on their territory.
With the protection provided by Singh on both the sides,
All the other Singhs joined their contingents after drinking water.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter, the Khalsa Singhs resumed fighting again, For protecting the helpless, defenceless Sikhs in the caravan. The Singhs started wielding their weapons once again, Who had returned so soon after quenching their thirst. (140)
lines: Thereafter, the Khalsa Singhs resumed fighting again,
For protecting the helpless, defenceless Sikhs in the caravan.
The Singhs started wielding their weapons once again,
Who had returned so soon after quenching their thirst.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Gilja Pathans, too, resolved to make use of water, Both the combatants drank water from the same source. Each soldier would return quietly after drinking water, As if they had forgotten to fight for the time-being. (141)
lines: As the Gilja Pathans, too, resolved to make use of water,
Both the combatants drank water from the same source.
Each soldier would return quietly after drinking water,
As if they had forgotten to fight for the time-being.

blocks.text: As the Singhs kept up the vigil and guarded their people, Even the wounded and incapacitated were carried along. As the caravan moved further for a distance of ten miles, Those separated and wounded also joined them here. (142)
lines: As the Singhs kept up the vigil and guarded their people,
Even the wounded and incapacitated were carried along.
As the caravan moved further for a distance of ten miles,
Those separated and wounded also joined them here.

blocks.text: In all twenty thousand Singhs could reach upto this point, While many others died or got scattered from the caravan. The eye-witnesses reckoned that there were one lakh Singhs, Fifty thousand of whom survived, the rest having perished in this massacre. (143)
lines: In all twenty thousand Singhs could reach upto this point,
While many others died or got scattered from the caravan.
The eye-witnesses reckoned that there were one lakh Singhs,
Fifty thousand of whom survived, the rest having perished in this massacre.

blocks.text: My father (S. Rai Singh) put the figure at thirty thousand Singhs, Who perished in this crusade the rest having returned safe. As both my (author's) father and uncle were part of this crusade, I have narrated this episode after listening this account from them. (144)
lines: My father (S.
Rai Singh) put the figure at thirty thousand Singhs,
Who perished in this crusade the rest having returned safe.
As both my (author's) father and uncle were part of this crusade,
I have narrated this episode after listening this account from them.

blocks.text: No head count of camels and horses could be kept, Which perished in this (most violent) massacre18 of the Sikhs. As the number of the dead could be more or less than this, I have recorded the number that my eyewitness father told. (145)
lines: No head count of camels and horses could be kept,
Which perished in this (most violent) massacre18 of the Sikhs.
As the number of the dead could be more or less than this,
I have recorded the number that my eyewitness father told.

blocks.text: Dohra:

At the end of this crusade, there did a Nihang Singh declare, In as loud a voice as could be heard by one and all. That Singhs who were Khalsas in letter and spirit survived, Those that were time-servers were purged and perished. (146)
lines: At the end of this crusade, there did a Nihang Singh declare,
In as loud a voice as could be heard by one and all.
That Singhs who were Khalsas in letter and spirit survived,
Those that were time-servers were purged and perished.

blocks.text: As most of the contingent chiefs had been wounded, There was hardly any one who remained in one piece. So many Singhs had, indeed, sacrificed in this crusade, That it was difficult to keep a head count of all those. (147)
lines: As most of the contingent chiefs had been wounded,
There was hardly any one who remained in one piece.
So many Singhs had, indeed, sacrificed in this crusade,
That it was difficult to keep a head count of all those.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Uncountable was the number of wounds which S. Charat Singh received, Innumerable were the arrows, lances and swords which hit his body. Whomsoever did S. Charat Singh hit like the mighty Bhim Sain19 , His every blow resulted in wounding his adversary in fight. (148)
lines: Uncountable was the number of wounds which S.
Charat Singh received,
Innumerable were the arrows, lances and swords which hit his body.
Whomsoever did S.
Charat Singh hit like the mighty Bhim Sain19 ,
His every blow resulted in wounding his adversary in fight.

blocks.text: Dohra:

From the concluding day of this massacre of the Sikhs, Did S. Charat Singh's stock sore high among the Singhs. Many a life of Sikhs in the caravan had he saved, Putting his own life at a great risk determinedly. (149)
lines: From the concluding day of this massacre of the Sikhs,
Did S.
Charat Singh's stock sore high among the Singhs.
Many a life of Sikhs in the caravan had he saved,
Putting his own life at a great risk determinedly.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Priase be to S. Charat Singh said each member of the caravan, They owed their life to S. Charat Singh's valorous deeds. Whosoever survived, survived because of S. Charat Singh's efforts, Thus did they praise S. Charat Singh all in one voice. (150)
lines: Priase be to S.
Charat Singh said each member of the caravan,
They owed their life to S.
Charat Singh's valorous deeds.
Whosoever survived, survived because of S.
Charat Singh's efforts,
Thus did they praise S.
Charat Singh all in one voice.

blocks.text: Thus did they bless him gathering in a congregational prayer, Undoubtedly would he be a chief among the Singhs. May he become a chief among the Khalsa Panth, Unitedly did they shower their blessings on this great Singh. (151)
lines: Thus did they bless him gathering in a congregational prayer,
Undoubtedly would he be a chief among the Singhs.
May he become a chief among the Khalsa Panth,
Unitedly did they shower their blessings on this great Singh.

blocks.text: Surely would he become a sovereign, some surmised, Undoubtedly would be occupy the Lahore throne, others opined. Admittedly would he take over Multan, some believed, Clearly would he conquer Kashmir and Kabul, others declared. (152)
lines: Surely would he become a sovereign, some surmised,
Undoubtedly would be occupy the Lahore throne, others opined.
Admittedly would he take over Multan, some believed,
Clearly would he conquer Kashmir and Kabul, others declared.

blocks.text: From Delhi to the South to the mountains in the East, Definitely would his writ shall run in all the directions. Thus did the whole caravan pray for S. Charat Singh, That the entire Khalsa Panth might accept his leadership. (153)
lines: From Delhi to the South to the mountains in the East,
Definitely would his writ shall run in all the directions.
Thus did the whole caravan pray for S.
Charat Singh,
That the entire Khalsa Panth might accept his leadership.

blocks.text: Dohra:

In whatever direction did S. Charat Singh move, Thither would the whole caravan follow in his foot steps. In great reverence did the Khalsa Panth hold him, Attributing the whole victory to S. Charat Singh's brave deeds. (154)
lines: In whatever direction did S.
Charat Singh move,
Thither would the whole caravan follow in his foot steps.
In great reverence did the Khalsa Panth hold him,
Attributing the whole victory to S.
Charat Singh's brave deeds.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Such great gratitude did he earn from the Khalsa Panth, That he would be the star attraction in every Sikh congregation. For each expedition would he be consulted in advance, Offerings in plenty would he be offered for his sacrifices. (155)
lines: Such great gratitude did he earn from the Khalsa Panth,
That he would be the star attraction in every Sikh congregation.
For each expedition would he be consulted in advance,
Offerings in plenty would he be offered for his sacrifices.
